Assertion B (bounded absence over the whole artifact): no non-comment line in ci.yml begins with `if:` or `continue-on-error:`. Matrix, all six inputs run against all three guards:
  input | shipped | A | B
  base  | GREEN   | GREEN | GREEN
  m1 (deadcode step deleted, TODO comment left)        | GREEN | RED   | GREEN
  m2 (wrapper -> bare go test, comment names wrapper)  | GREEN | RED   | GREEN

A and B together turn every one of §1.1's five inputs RED while both stay GREEN on the shipped ci.yml. A is ~60 lines in the same test file; B is 15.
note: The guard is repairable against every input §1.1 measures, and by two assertions in the two shapes §1.1's OWN table calls immune — A moves the subject from the whole file to the parsed run-block (bounded, and compared for equality, so no mention can satisfy it), B is the bottom-left absence cell over the whole of one bounded artifact. What §1.1 actually establishes is narrower and correct: an unstructured `strings.Contains` over the file text cannot work, and that is a weakness in the assertion's SCOPE, not a proof that no assertion exists. evidence: CUT unit — snapshot line 97, 'It is the same resolution and the same executor a task close uses.' It presupposes there is ONE executor a task close uses. evidence: && does not collapse exit codes; it propagates the first failing command's status verbatim. Shell: sh -c 'true && exit 7' -> 7; sh -c '(exit 3) && (exit 9)' -> 3; a loop over codes 1,2,3,4,5,42 in the middle of a three-link chain reports each one back unchanged. End to end through tp itself, in a scratch project at /tmp/tp-ground-1470/qa whose quality_gate is a four-link && chain with a third link exiting 33: tp done emits code 4, exit_code 33, gate_cmd the full chain, output_tail [step1-ok, step2-ok, step3-failing]. engine.RunCommand (internal/engine/runcmd.go:96) takes the code straight off exec.ExitError.
note: The conclusion — that a named entry should carry its own exit code — survives; the reason given for it does not, and the reason is the whole of the sentence's argument. Today's string gate ALREADY reports the failing step's own exit code (33, not 1), and the output tail already ends at the failing step. What the array buys is the entry NAME and a structured per-entry record, not the exit code. This matters because §3 (u37) and test row 4 (u68) both rest on it, and row 1 (u65) names a mutant that therefore cannot fail.
